title: Maximum Weight Node
body:
A maze has N cells numbered 0 to N − 1. Each cell has at most one exit: edge[i] is the cell you reach by leaving cell i, or -1 if cell i has no exit.

The weight of a cell is the sum of the numbers of all cells whose exit points to it. Print the cell with the largest weight. If several cells tie, print the one with the largest number.

The report did not capture the tie rule; the largest-number rule is the one used in the commonly shared version of this question.

Function to complete

Complete maxWeightNode(edge). It returns the cell with the largest weight (the larger index on a tie).

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.

samples.ex: Nobody points anywhere, so every weight is 0 and the largest cell number wins.

py.pre:
from typing import *
import sys, math, collections, heapq, bisect, itertools, functools
from collections import *
py.post:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    _n = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    edge = list(map(int, _t[_p:_p + (_n)])); _p += (_n)
    _r = Solution().maxWeightNode(edge)
    print(_r)
